subject: Copywriting
title: Super Bowl Ads: Copywriting's Biggest Stage
description: A fast breakdown of Super Bowl Ads: Copywriting's Biggest Stage for builders.

hook.text: A 30-second Super Bowl ad costs $7 million. More people discuss the ads than the game itself.

buildup.text: Apple's 1984 ad launched the Macintosh during the Super Bowl. It aired once and became advertising legend.

discovery.text: Super Bowl ads proved that entertainment sells. The best ones tell stories, not features.

twist.text: Many $7M ads flop. Being expensive doesn't mean being good. A bad script wastes millions in seconds.

climax.text: Budweiser's Clydesdales, Old Spice's 'The Man,' Doritos' fan-made ads—all Super Bowl copy hall of fame.

punchline.text: $7M for 30 seconds. The stakes make the copy sharper.

quiz.question: Which brand's 1984 Super Bowl ad became a legendary advertising moment?

details.summary: The Super Bowl became advertising's premier showcase, with 30-second spots costing over $7 million by the 2020s. Apple's 1984 commercial, Budweiser's Clydesdales, and countless others proved that the Super Bowl was where brands could reach 100+ million viewers and create cultural moments through...
details.whyItMatters: Super Bowl ads represent the pinnacle of advertising craft — maximum budget, maximum audience, maximum pressure. Studying them reveals what brands believe their best creative work looks like.
takeaways: Super Bowl ad slots cost over $7 million for 30 seconds
Brands create their most ambitious work for this unique mass audience
The event is the only time consumers actively seek out and share ads

faq.question: Why do brands spend so much on Super Bowl ads?
faq.answer: The Super Bowl is the last remaining mass-audience event in fragmented media. It reaches 100+ million engaged viewers simultaneously. More importantly, it's the only advertising context where people actively watch, discuss, and share ads — generating massive earned media.

faq.question: What makes a Super Bowl ad memorable?
faq.answer: The highest-rated Super Bowl ads combine emotional storytelling with surprise. They often avoid product focus in favor of brand values. Humor, nostalgia, and cultural relevance consistently outperform product demonstrations in viewer recall and sharing.
